text:
Buffalo comes into Anaheim on a high note after a 2-0 win in San Jose that snapped a three-game winless run, with Colten Ellis stopping all 23 shots. It's game three of a four-game road trip, and the Sabres are missing Konsta Helenius, Jiri Kulich and Matt Grzelcyk. They're also back in Olen Zellweger's old building, his first visit since leaving the Ducks after 164 games. Anaheim lost 6-5 in overtime to Vancouver, a team that came back from three goals down to end a ten-game winless run. The Ducks are 1-3-1 in their last five without Pavel Mintyukov and Ryan Poehling, and Roger McQueen has taken Poehling's spot beside Nesterenko and Killorn.

Our numbers favor the Sabres slightly, 3.29 expected goals (the quality of chances) to 2.97. BUF has taken 52% of the expected goals at five on five, ANA 44%, and Buffalo's record is worse than its play: a -7 goal difference on +1.3 expected. Anaheim takes 4.8 penalties a game, which keeps feeding opponents power plays. Projected goalie Ellis sits at +3.2 goals saved above expected this season (how many goals he's stopped beyond what the shots called for) against +0.3 for Lukas Dostal, who was at -3.7 last year.

Tage Thompson is our top Sabre at 68% for a point, and Zach Benson, a "total maniac" in Joe Yerdon's words for Bleacher Report, is 27% to score. For Anaheim, Cutter Gauthier hasn't scored in nine games despite 3.2 expected goals and is 34% to score, while Leo Carlsson is 71% for a point. Our under-the-radar pick is Noah Ostlund, 50% for a point as the Ducks give up the third-most expected goals per 60.
